This page builds one reusable source snapshot for the [Palace](tutorial-xmon-palace.qmd)
and [AEDT](tutorial-xmon-aedt.qmd) workflows. It starts from OrPen's public
Kosen2024 Xmon preview cell and ground-short coupon. The cell is an independent
parametric adaptation of Kosen et al., [PRX Quantum 5, 030350
(2024)](https://doi.org/10.1103/PRXQuantum.5.030350), shared under
[CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); it is not an
author-supplied mask. The dimensions and coupon settings follow the public
Palace Route B example linked from [Examples](examples.qmd); they are public
simulation inputs, not measured device data or paper-mask dimensions. Use the
matched SCGSim and OrPen versions listed there. Quarto shows this code without
executing it.

## Build the component and named coupon occurrences

The device component owns local Entity IDs for its pad and couplers, the
junction port, and source geometry. Its junction ground arm is a local metal
contribution to the root D1 plane, not a separate conductor Entity. The
`place_flip_chip_ground_short_bumps` helper returns a final coupon with named
device and bump references and one root-local D0/D1 ground-plane pair, authored
by OrPen's `author_common_flip_chip_ground_planes` helper. Register the actual
device and bump references by their names; do not reconstruct hierarchy from
flattened polygon names.

```python
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib
import json

import gdsfactory as gf
import orpen_sc_pdk
from orpen_sc_pdk import LAYER_STACK, get_material_records
from orpen_sc_pdk.helpers.assembly import place_flip_chip_ground_short_bumps
from orpen_sc_pdk.tech import OUTER_VACUUM_THICKNESS_UM
from scgsim.sgb import GeometryPlan, build_gds_stack_geometry_input

output_dir = Path.cwd() / ".artifacts" / "public-xmon-inputs"
output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
gds_path = output_dir / "xmon.gds"
stack_path = output_dir / "xmon.stack.json"

orpen_sc_pdk.activate()
gf.clear_cache()
device = gf.get_component(
    "kosen2024_flip_chip_xmon_qubit",
    bump_ring_count_per_side=0,
    qubit_pad_length=309.5,
    qubit_pad_width=24.65,
    qubit_gap=20.0,
)
coupon = place_flip_chip_ground_short_bumps(
    device,
    coupon_padding_um=75.0,
    clearance_um=30.0,
    placement_mode="corner_anchors",
)
component = coupon.component
```

The zero ring count leaves the public device's authored coupon shorts as the
only bump instances. The helper may increase `coupon_padding_um` to fit them;
`coupon.stack_coupon_padding_um` is the corresponding stack value. The common
planes belong to the final coupon, while the device's local ground-arm
contribution is resolved against its named occurrence and included in D1.
The component, layer stack, and material records come from OrPen. SCGSim does
not author a second copy of those PDK facts.

## Assign the final Net map and prepare one snapshot

The component's local Entity IDs are scoped by their occurrence paths. This
example places the root D0 and D1 planes, four device couplers, and eight
sibling shorts on `Ground`, and the device's `D1_XMON_PAD` Entity on
`xmon_pad`. The local junction ground arm is already included in the root D1
plane, so it is not listed as a separate Net member. The final Net assignment
is a Notebook operation on `GeometryPlan`. Entity IDs preserve source lineage;
they do not create one measurement or field expression per Entity. Physical
mesh groups are separate computational aggregates: the eight same-role,
same-material Ground bump Entities share one physical group while remaining
eight qualified Entity members. AEDT's EPR owner/interface/integral grouping
remains its own backend contract.

```python
plan = GeometryPlan(
    component=component,
    root_id="chip",
    layer_stack=LAYER_STACK,
    material_records=get_material_records(),
    coupon_padding_um=coupon.stack_coupon_padding_um,
)
for name, reference in coupon.named_instances.items():
    plan.register_instance(f"chip/{name}", reference)

plan.set_nets({
    "xmon_pad": ("chip/device/D1_XMON_PAD",),
    "Ground": (
        "chip/D0_TOP_GROUND_PLANE",
        "chip/D1_BOTTOM_GROUND_PLANE",
        *(f"chip/device/D1_COUPLER_{index}" for index in range(1, 5)),
        *(
            f"chip/{name}/D0_D1_INDIUM_BUMP"
            for name in coupon.named_instances
            if name.startswith("short_")
        ),
    ),
})
plan.set_vacuum_region(
    padding=(0.0, 0.0, float(OUTER_VACUUM_THICKNESS_UM))
)
snapshot = plan.prepare()
```

The outer Region padding is an explicit shared input, not a backend-specific
override. The authored `D0_TO_D1_GAP` remains its own vacuum Entity. Palace and
AEDT choose different external boundary defaults; matching source geometry
does not make those physical models identical.

## Save and reread the GDS plus stack

`GeometryPlanSnapshot.gds_bytes` and the detached `snapshot.stack` provide a
portable GDS/JSON pair. The public SGB reader can load that pair independently
of the live component references. This round trip checks the emitted GDS hash
and qualified Entity identities; it does not validate native solver geometry.

```python
gds_path.write_bytes(snapshot.gds_bytes)
stack_path.write_text(
    json.dumps(snapshot.stack, sort_keys=True, indent=2),
    encoding="utf-8",
)

reloaded = build_gds_stack_geometry_input(
    gds_file=gds_path,
    stack_file=stack_path,
    top_cell_name=snapshot.stack["metadata"]["top_cell_name"],
)
actual_gds_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(gds_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
if actual_gds_sha256 != snapshot.gds_sha256:
    raise ValueError("GDS/stack round trip changed the source GDS identity")
if reloaded.metadata["gds_sha256"] != actual_gds_sha256:
    raise ValueError("the detached stack does not identify these GDS bytes")
if {item.semantic_id for item in reloaded.entities} != {
    item.semantic_id for item in snapshot.geometry_input.entities
}:
    raise ValueError("GDS/stack round trip changed qualified Entity identities")

port_name = "chip/device/o_junction_lumped"
port_sheets = [
    item for item in snapshot.geometry_input.port_sheet_regions
    if item.metadata.get("source_name") == port_name
]
if len(port_sheets) != 1:
    raise ValueError(f"expected one authored source sheet for {port_name!r}")
port_sheet = port_sheets[0]
if len(port_sheet.overlaps) != 2:
    raise ValueError("the authored junction sheet must overlap two terminal owners")
print(gds_path, stack_path, snapshot.gds_sha256)
```

The shared variable `snapshot` is ready for either backend page. The source
sheet ID and its two owner overlaps come from the actual prepared port record;
the examples do not invent a polygon ID or junction geometry. See the
[GeometryPlan contract](geometry-sgb.qmd#component-to-backend-geometry-contract)
for identity, grouping, and validation boundaries.
